verdict: United Rentals rode booming specialty demand to record revenue of $4.9B, up 16%, and a 35% jump in earnings per share — a bigger fleet, used more of the time, at better margins.

segments.name: General Rentals
segments.note: Everyday construction and industrial equipment rental — the core fleet business, up 8.5% YoY.

segments.name: Specialty
segments.note: Trench safety, power, climate and fluid solutions — specialty revenue surged 30.3% YoY on a bigger fleet and strong demand.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and running the branch network and head office.

opex.name: Non-rental depreciation
opex.note: Depreciation and amortization on everything except the rental fleet (fleet depreciation sits in cost of revenue).

opex.name: Restructuring charge
opex.note: A one-off restructuring charge taken this quarter.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $184M, partly offset by $6M of other income, for a net cost of $178M.
oneTimers: The quarter includes a $15M restructuring charge in operating expenses. Adjusted EPS was $15.55 vs $14.77 GAAP.

takeaways.title: Specialty is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Specialty rentals — trench, power, climate and fluids — grew 30.3% to $1.83B and now bring in 37% of revenue, at a richer 47.6% rentals gross margin.

takeaways.title: Record profit
takeaways.text: Net income was a record $920M, an 18.8% margin, and adjusted EBITDA reached $2.33B — 47.6 cents of every revenue dollar before interest, tax and depreciation.

takeaways.title: EPS up 35%
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose to $14.77 from $10.91, helped by growth and by buybacks — the company returned $1.5B to shareholders in the first nine months.

follow100Note: The breakdown rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.
